title: Tundra Glow A-Z
hook: Low light makes small colors matter more.
roundStructure: Round 1 lexical-semantic A-Z; Round 2 retrieval-action A-Z; 4+4+4+4+4+4+2 chunks
visualStyle: soft 3D tundra storybook, pale blue lavender and snow white, gentle light, crisp simple subjects

creativeFingerprint.pointOfView: a child learning to see subtle color and contrast in snow, tundra and cold water
creativeFingerprint.chorusFunction: restate pale-dark-blue contrast without turning the song into a glitter effect
creativeFingerprint.grooveMeter: slow open 6/8 with held reflected-light phrases
creativeFingerprint.round1Grammar: hand-written color-and-light observations; facts stay concrete and not every target is described as white or glowing
creativeFingerprint.round2Grammar: light/contrast cue -> recall beat -> target -> gentle point/shape gesture
creativeFingerprint.sectionContrast: Verses stay sparse; chorus widens; retrieval strips back. soft bell sparkle after targets over a warm acoustic pulse
creativeFingerprint.signatureColor: soft bell sparkle after targets over a warm acoustic pulse
creativeFingerprint.authorialIntent: Use reflected polar light as the organizing image: snow, floe, pale animals, dark birds and open water change how color is noticed in a low-light tundra world.
creativeFingerprint.lyricIdentity: A quiet child observer watches contrast rather than sparkle clichés; recurring language uses pale, blue-shadow, low sun, dark-on-white, reflection, soft edge and glow.
semanticArc: dark and bright animals sharpen the scene
sea and ice reflect different color
blue evening closes with small warm details
forbiddenGenericLanguage: ice and snow shine back to me
